chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent me to Yemen and said to me:
'O Ali, do not fight anyone until you call him (to Islam).
And I swear by God, that God should guide one man through your hands is better for you than all that the sun rises upon and sets, and his wilayah belongs to you, O Ali.'

key_terms.الْيَمَنِ: Yemen, a region of the Arabian Peninsula where Ali was dispatched as a judge and missionary
key_terms.تَدْعُوَهُ: You call him — da'wa (invitation to Islam) must precede any armed conflict
key_terms.تُقَاتِلَنَّ: Fight/wage war — the emphatic prohibition form lā tufātilannal emphasizes absolute prohibition
key_terms.وَايْمُ اللَّهِ: A pre-Islamic Arabic oath formula meaning 'I swear by God,' expressing the highest sincerity
key_terms.وَلَاؤُهُ: Wilayah, meaning loyalty, guardianship, or allegiance — a key theological concept in Shia Islam
key_terms.يَدَيْكَ: Your two hands — idiomatic for 'through your agency/effort'

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to Imam Ali before sending him to Yemen?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts Imam Ali (AS) narrating the Prophet's instructions before sending him on a mission to Yemen. The Prophet (SAWW) commanded Ali not to engage in combat with any people until he first invited them to Islam, establishing da'wa (invitation) as a prerequisite to jihad. The Prophet then emphasized this principle with a powerful oath: guiding even a single person to Islam through peaceful invitation is more valuable than the entire world — a teaching that underscores the primacy of guidance and the sanctity of human life in Islamic military ethics.
